answer: Stake-bonded identity defeats Sybils: every agent must lock its own collateral, and detected fraud slashes that bond. Because voting weight grows only with the square root of locked stake, splitting a fixed budget across many fake identities earns no extra influence, so cloning is pointless. The frozen stake is a glacier that melts only under penalties; flooding a meadow with duplicate agents still demands fresh capital per clone. Each spiral of new Sybil identities raises the attacker's upfront cost faster than any payoff, making mass impersonation uneconomical.
